_comment: Where a package's release-readiness list lives -- POINTERS, not the lists.
A list's reasoning belongs with the plan that produced it; duplicating it
here would give a cut two sources that can disagree. What this file buys is
that `bin/release-helper.sh check` names the list instead of relying on
An entry names the SECTION, not the file that holds it: `heading` is the
whole pointer and the check is a search of the tree for it. A path would
be a citation into a tree most clones do not have, and it would need an
edit every time that tree reorganized; a heading needs none, and a
section that merely moved still resolves.
A package with no entry has nothing outstanding and prints nothing. An
entry whose heading is in no document in a tree that IS present prints a
drift warning, so a renamed or deleted section is reported rather than
quietly pointing at nothing -- and an entry whose heading is found in
MORE than one document prints an ambiguity warning, because a heading
that no longer identifies one section has stopped being a pointer.
